old_caption:
The video captures a close-up view of a coffee brewing process using a pour-over method. The scene is set on a clean, white countertop where a person, partially visible from the waist down, stands to the right side of the frame. They are wearing a green shirt and beige pants. A black electric kettle with a digital display showing "97" is positioned to the left, indicating the temperature of the water being used for brewing.

In the center of the frame, a clear glass pour-over dripper sits atop a black base, holding a cone-shaped filter filled with ground coffee. A stream of hot water is being poured into the filter from a gooseneck kettle held by an unseen hand, creating ripples and bubbles in the coffee grounds. Steam rises gently from the coffee, adding a sense of warmth and activity to the scene. To the left of the dripper, a wooden-handled brush rests on the counter, likely used for cleaning or preparing the coffee setup.

caption:
The video captures an overhead close-up of a pour-over coffee setup on a white table. A person, visible only as a torso in a dark green shirt and khaki trousers, holds a gooseneck kettle above a cone dripper lined with a paper filter and filled with blooming coffee grounds. The dripper rests on a glass carafe on a black digital scale, while a black device with a blue "97" readout and a wooden-handled brush lie to the left.

A thin water stream falls from the kettle spout onto the coffee bed, its landing point tracing a slow circular pattern—center, then right, then left, then center again—as the person shifts the spout. The foam bloom deforms with each pass: bubbles agitate, the darker central patch spreads and contracts, and the edge ring reshapes. In a few moments the thin stream drops out of view, then reappears. The dark liquid in the carafe stays roughly stable, while the props and the blue readout remain fixed.

Pouring.
